summary: Configured and verified persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1. Seven compressed rotations are retained, open writers continue after rotation, and the setup survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Confirmed the system's persistent daily logrotate timer processes /etc/logrotate.d.
Performed a real rotation while a process held the log open; the same descriptor wrote successfully afterward.
Verified the resulting gzip archive and active log data.
Safely rebooted node1 exactly once and verified its boot identity changed, services recovered, configuration and archived data persisted, and the active log remained writable.

evidence.summary: The effective production rule reports rotation after one day; logrotate.timer is enabled, active, persistent, and scheduled daily.
The exercised rotation used rotateCount 7 and gzip; archive integrity passed, and the post-reboot effective rule still reports seven rotations.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A held-open writer remained on inode 290760 across copy-truncate and successfully wrote continuity-after-rotation into the active log.

Healthy baseline boot ID f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, node1 returned with boot ID 846f820f-5243-4899-97ae-5af0d3f12fc6, and post-restart checks showed a running system, active/enabled timer, zero failed units, matching configuration/archive checksums, and a writable recovered log.
